title: [DOC-7] Records-retention law is stated incorrectly or without a hedge in the regulator and counse
description: Review finding DOC-7: Records-retention law is stated incorrectly or without a hedge in the regulator and counsel guides (lens DOC). Location: guides/counsel.md:10, :206, :250; guides/regulators.md:248, :253, :258, :301, :375; profiles/purview-bridge.md:620. Fix: The text of 17 CFR 240.17a-4(b) says "not less than three years, the first two years in an easily accessible place", and (b)(4) covers "all communications received and ... sent". The rule contains no seven-year period. Its periods are six years ((a), (c), some of (e)), three years ((b)), and life of the enterprise ((d)). regulators:248 "seven years for certain records" is therefore wrong. Its "six-year ... most records" misattributes 17a-4(a) to communications. 17a-4(f)(2)(i)(A) allows "a complete time-stamped audit trail" as an alternative to (B) "non-rewriteable, non-erasable format", so regulators:375 "requires WORM" is wrong after the 2022 amendments. The hash-chain argument at :375 fits the audit-trail alternative better and should be framed that way. I found no FINRA vendor-registration regime. The 2022 amendments use a "designated third party" or "designated executive officer" (Dechert, ACA summaries). I could not find a source that proves the negative, so hedge rather than assert: replace "FINRA-registered" with "qualified third-party archiving vendor (or the firm's designated third party under 17a-4(f))".
